steps: Sift the flour and 1 tsp of the salt into a large bowl. Push 1 hard-boiled egg yolk through a fine sieve into it, add 1 raw egg and mix well. Beat in 5 tbsp of the butter, 1 tbsp at a time.
Knead the dough on a floured surface until smooth, wrap it and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onion and rutabaga for about 5 minutes, until soft. Grind or very finely chop them with the cooked beef.

Melt the rest of the butter, add the meat mixture and cook over low heat, stirring now and then, until dry and thick. Let it cool, then stir in 1 beaten egg and season with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Roll the dough into a 13 x 8-inch rectangle. Spoon the filling down the middle, wet the long edges and fold them over the filling, then fold in the ends.
Put it seam side down on a baking sheet, brush with the last egg, beaten, and bake for about 30 minutes, until golden. Cut it diagonally into 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Melt half of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook half of the chopped onion for about 5 minutes. Add the drained sauerkraut, cook for 5 minutes more, season and let it cool.
Melt the rest of the butter, cook the rest of the onion until translucent and stir it into the mashed potatoes. Season.
For the dough, beat the eggs with the sour cream. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder together, stir them in and knead on a floured surface until smooth and firm.

Roll half of the dough out 1/8 inch thick and cut 3-inch rounds. Put a small spoonful of potato filling in the middle of each, wet the edges, fold over and seal with a fork. Repeat with the rest of the dough and the sauerkraut filling.
Cook the pierogi in a large pot of lightly salted boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, until they float. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Cook the pasta as the package says.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the chopped onion, garlic and chili for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the pilchards with their sauce, breaking up the fish with a spoon, then add the olives and cook for a few minutes more.
Drain the pasta and add it to the pan with 2 to 3 tbsp of the cooking water. Toss well and serve scattered with parmesan.
Blend the chilies, garlic, ginger, oregano, coriander, paprika, 2 tbsp of the vinegar and the oil into a marinade. Rub it over the chicken and leave it for 1 hour at room temperature.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roast the chicken in a roasting pan for 1 hour 20 minutes, then let it rest under loose foil for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, for the slaw, mix the thinly sliced red onion, the grated carrots and beet and the shredded cabbage with the mayonnaise, yogurt, cumin seeds and the rest of the vinegar. Season.
Serve the chicken with the slaw.

Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole or cast-iron skillet over low heat. Add the chopped onions with a pinch of salt, cover and cook gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then. Add the garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the sliced peppers and cook, covered, over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until just tender.
Stir in the oregano, thyme, bay leaves and some salt and pepper. Add the diced zucchini and eggplant, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Make 4 hollows and carefully crack an egg into each. Cook over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until the eggs are set but still a little soft. Scatter with parsley and serve.
Chop the pepper, onion and tomato.
Heat a little olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic, tomato and pepper with the achiote paste, cumin, oregano, salt and pepper for about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for about 2 minutes on each side.

Pour in the broth, cover and simmer over low heat for about 35 minutes, until the chicken is very tender. (In a pressure cooker, cook on high for 20 minutes.) Add salt if needed and serve with rice and beans.
Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, honey and thyme leaves in a large bowl and season well.
Add the lettuce, halved tomatoes, sliced green onions and chopped chili and toss.
Take the seeds out of the pomegranate over a bowl and remove any white pith.
Arrange the salad on a platter and scatter with the pomegranate seeds and crumbled feta.
Heat the oven to 275°F (140°C). Heat the goose fat in a large ovenproof pan with a tight lid over high heat and brown the diced pork for a few minutes.
Lower the heat and add the sliced onion, whole garlic cloves, sliced carrot and fennel seeds. Cook gently for a few minutes to soften.
Pour in the vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pan. Add the broth, tomato paste and half of the rosemary and parsley. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes, then season.
Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours, taking the lid off for the last hour. Stir now and then, and add the drained beans for the last 30 minutes.
Heat the broiler. Scatter the rest of the herbs and the breadcrumbs over the top, drizzle with a little oil and broil for 5 to 10 minutes, until golden. Serve with crusty bread and broccoli.
Cut each pork tenderloin into 5 pieces. Put each piece in a plastic bag and pound it with a rolling pin into a thin cutlet.
Mix the wine, paprika, salt, pepper and the juice of half a lemon, add the pork and marinate for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch fries, soak them in cold water for 5 minutes, change the water and soak for 5 minutes more. Drain and pat dry.

Heat the oil in a deep pan to 265°F (130°C) and fry the potatoes in batches for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain. Heat the oil to 350°F (180°C) and fry them again for about 3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Drain and salt.
Rub the pork with olive oil and cook it on a very hot grill pan or barbecue for 1 minute on each side, in 2 batches.
Pile the fries on plates, top with the pork and its juices, and serve with mayonnaise and lemon wedges.
Rub the steaks with the cut garlic, put them in a bag with the olive oil, 1 tbsp of the vinegar and the parsley stalks, and pound them a few times with a rolling pin. Leave for 1 to 2 hours.
For the green sauce, blend the basil, jalapeño, green onions, sugar, the rest of the vinegar and 1 tbsp of water until smooth.
Heat a grill pan or frying pan until very hot. Brush off the garlic and parsley, season the steaks and sear them for 2 minutes on each side. Let them rest on a plate.
Toast the cut ciabatta halves and press them into the steak juices on the plate.
Slice the steaks and put them in the rolls with the green sauce and arugula.
Thinly slice the potatoes and boil them for 5 to 8 minutes, until firm but not soft.
Meanwhile, put the sliced onions in a baking dish with the olive oil and broth and cook in a 400°F (200°C) oven or on the stove until soft.
Drain the potatoes and spread them over the onions. Season and spoon over the crème fraîche to cover. Grate parmesan over the top and broil until golden.
Meanwhile, season the chicken and cook it in a frying pan for 5 to 7 minutes on each side, with the bacon, until cooked through.
Serve the gratin with the chicken and bacon, and with peas and spinach if you like.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the water, chopped onion, olive oil, vinegar, mustard, crushed garlic, black pepper, cayenne and salt in a roasting dish.
Add the chicken and turn it until well coated.
Roast for about 1 1/2 hours, basting now and then, until it reaches 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh.
Cut the potatoes into fries and pat them dry. Heat oil for deep-frying to 365°F (185°C).
Warm the gravy in a saucepan.
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes, until golden, and drain on paper towels.
Pile the fries on a platter, scatter the cheese curds over them, ladle the hot gravy over the top and serve right away.
Whisk 5 eggs in each of two bowls and season. Fry the sliced zucchini and green onions gently in the oil for about 10 minutes, until soft. Let them cool and stir them into one bowl.
Add the roasted, sliced peppers, the crushed garlic and the chopped chili to the other bowl and season.

Heat a little oil in an 8 to 9-inch non-stick frying pan. Pour in a third of the zucchini mixture and cook until set and lightly browned underneath, then flip it with a plate and cook the other side. Make 2 more, then 3 with the pepper mixture.
Beat the cream cheese with the milk until spreadable and stir in the chives, basil, salt and pepper.

Line a deep round cake pan the same size as the frying pan with plastic wrap. Layer the omelettes, alternating colors, with a thin layer of cheese between each. Cover and chill for a few hours or up to 24 hours.
Turn it out onto a plate, top with arugula, shaved parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil and black pepper, and cut into wedges.
Lower the egg into boiling water and cook for 6 1/2 to 7 minutes. Put it in ice water for 3 to 5 minutes, then peel it.
Bring the 2 cups of water to a boil and cook the noodles as the package says.
Stir in the soy sauce, chilli sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour into a bowl, top with the egg cut in half and the sliced green onions, and serve.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a 10 x 14-inch baking pan.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onions for about 5 minutes, then over low heat for about 40 minutes more, stirring, until very soft and dark brown.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pot, add the chicken, lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Peel and finely grate the potatoes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean towel. Mix in the salt and pepper and enough hot broth to make a mixture like oatmeal.
Spread half of the potatoes in the pan, lay the sliced chicken over them, scatter with the onions and cover with the rest of the potatoes.
Bake for about 1 hour, until golden brown. Serve with a little of the reheated broth poured over each portion.
Simmer the pork knuckle in water for about 3 hours, until the meat falls off the bone. Lift out the pork and keep the broth.
Meanwhile, boil half of the potatoes, peel them when cool and mash them well with no lumps. Peel and finely grate the rest and pat them dry with paper towels.
Mix the grated and mashed potatoes, then mix in the flour and salt with your hands.
Bring the pork broth to a very gentle simmer with the stock cubes (it mustn't boil hard). With a tablespoon dipped in cold water, shape smooth balls and drop them into the broth.

Simmer them for about 30 minutes, heating the sausage in the same pot. Meanwhile, boil the chopped rutabaga and carrots for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain and mash them with the cream, butter and nutmeg.
Serve the dumplings with the meat, the mash and chopped parsley.
Soak the dried chilies, ginger, garlic, pepper, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and tamarind in the vinegar with the sugar, turmeric and a pinch of salt for 35 to 40 minutes.
Grind it all into a thick, smooth paste, adding a little more vinegar only if needed. It must stay thick to stick to the fish.
Rinse the mackerel, slit them open down the middle and cut a few slashes on top. Fill the slit and slashes with the paste and coat the fish all over. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a shallow pan and fry the fish until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with salad, lime wedges and rice.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large ovenproof pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, celery and garlic, season and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.

Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C). Add the drained beans, the tomatoes with their juice, the water, rosemary and thyme. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes.
Remove the herb stems and stir in the chopped kale. Taste and season.
Lay the bread over the top of the soup, scatter with the sliced red onion, drizzle with the rest of the oil and sprinkle with the parmesan.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the bread, onions and cheese are browned and crisp. Serve in bowls.
Soak the dried kidney beans overnight, drain them, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 1 hour, until tender.
Add the rice, coconut milk, chopped onion, pepper and salt, with enough water to just cover everything.
Lay the whole Scotch bonnets on top, taking care not to burst them, and simmer covered for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Remove the peppers before serving.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan with a lid and fry the sausages, cut into pieces, over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, until browned. Set them aside.

Fry the chopped onion and fennel in the pan for 15 minutes, until soft and caramelized. Add the paprika, garlic and half of the fennel seeds for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and boil for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, sugar, 1/2 cup (100 ml) of water, the sausages and 1/2 tsp of salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, taking the lid off after 10 minutes, until thick. Stir in the olives and the rest of the fennel seeds.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water for 12 to 14 minutes, until al dente. Drain and stir in 1 tbsp of oil.
For the pesto, blend the pecorino, anchovy, the rest of the oil and 1 tbsp of water into a rough paste, then add the basil and pulse briefly.
Serve the pasta with the sauce and a spoonful of pesto on top.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice the eggplants, brush them with 1 tbsp of the oil, season and roast on a baking sheet for 20 minutes, until browned, adding the tomatoes for the last 5 minutes.
Tear the pita into pieces and toast it on another sheet for about 8 minutes, until crisp.
For the dressing, mix the vinegar, chopped mint, 1 chopped shallot, the chopped chili, the rest of the oil and some salt and pepper.
Put the eggplant, tomatoes, the other shallot, sliced, and the toasted pita in a bowl. Pour over the dressing, crumble the goat cheese on top and add the arugula.

Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chopped fennel, eggplant, pepper and zucchini with a little olive oil, salt and pepper and roast for about 20 minutes, turning a couple of times, until golden and almost cooked.
Meanwhile, heat a little olive oil in a paella pan or large frying pan over low-medium heat and cook the chopped onion for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft.

Turn up the heat to medium, stir in the rice, paprika and saffron for 1 minute, then add the wine and reduce by half. Stir in two thirds of the broth and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring a couple of times.
Stir in the peas, season and gently mix in the roasted vegetables. Pour in the rest of the broth, lay lemon wedges on top, cover and cook for 10 minutes more.
Turn up the heat until you hear a slight crackle, to toast the bottom. Take it off the heat, let it sit for 5 minutes and sprinkle with parsley.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the chopped carrots, celery and onion for about 4 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, bay leaves, water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, partly cover and cook for about 30 minutes, until tender, adding water if needed. Uncover, stir in the vinegar, let it reduce a little and season.

Meanwhile, cut the eggplants in half, score the flesh in a crisscross pattern and put them cut side up on a lined baking sheet. Brush each half with about 1 tbsp of oil, season and put a rosemary sprig on top. Roast for 25 to 35 minutes, until very tender and charred.
Toast the pine nuts in a little oil in a skillet for about 4 minutes, until golden. Thin the tahini with a little water, lemon or vinegar and salt to make a sauce.
Stir half of the parsley into the lentils, put them on a platter and lay the eggplant on top. Spoon the tahini sauce over, and sprinkle with the pine nuts and the rest of the parsley.
Halve the cabbage, cut out the tough core and slice it thinly.

Put it in a large pan with everything else except the sausages: the oil, butter, sliced onion, vinegar, sugar, chopped chili, rosemary and diced apple. Add 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) of water and some salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring often and adding a little water if it gets dry.
Add the sausages, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, then uncover and cook for 10 minutes more. Serve with mashed or boiled potatoes.
Put the chicken in a large pot, cover with water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, skimming off any foam so the broth stays clear.
For the last hour, add the onions, carrots, leek, celery and cabbage, the cloves, allspice, bay leaves, parsley, dill, pepper and salt.
Strain the broth. Pull the chicken off the bones in large chunks and slice the carrots.
Return the chicken and carrots to the broth and serve hot.
Mix the beef, chopped onion, eggs, chopped chili, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat a little oil in a pan or on a griddle and pour in the mixture.
Press the baguette, split open, cut side down on top and cook for about 2 minutes, until the egg sets.
Turn it over to crisp the bread a little. Add mayonnaise, cut it into pieces and serve.
For the hollandaise, whisk the lemon juice, 1 tsp of the vinegar and 3 of the egg yolks in a bowl until light and frothy. Set the bowl over a pan of simmering water and whisk until it thickens.
Gradually whisk in all but 1 tbsp of the butter, melted, until thick. If it looks like it's splitting, whisk it off the heat for a few minutes. Season and keep warm.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil, add the rest of the vinegar and lower the heat to a gentle simmer. Stir to make a slight whirlpool and slide in the other 4 eggs one at a time. Poach each for about 4 minutes and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Split, toast and butter the muffins. Put a couple of slices of salmon on each half, top with an egg and spoon over the hollandaise.
